Published online:
2026-08-31

Geographic focus:
Asia (India), Africa (East & West Africa), Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Yemen/Red Sea), Europe (indirect reference)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — August shipment data, Jazan refinery cuts, year-ago ME market share figures
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — Near-term arbitrage viability, continued Houthi blockade threat, Asian refinery run trajectory
T3. Long-term development [NO] — No structural/multi-year outlook discussed

Synopsis:
Asia's diesel exports to Africa are hitting a 4.5-year high in August 2026 (~1.8–2.0 MMT), filling the void left by collapsing Middle Eastern supply (~0.6–0.8 MMT, a near 9-year low). The root cause is the US-Iran war, the Houthi blockade of the Red Sea, and direct attacks on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery — which has zeroed out its Africa-bound shipments. A widening east-west spread (−$135/t vs. −$100/t in July) is incentivising Asian and Indian traders to divert westward. Strong Asian refiner margins ($66/bbl) are sustaining output. The arbitrage flow is expected to continue as long as Saudi tankers avoid Bab el-Mandeb and European supply remains tight.
